title: Go: API Gateway
description: Build an API gateway with route matching, path parameters, request transformation, service aggregation, caching, and rate limiting.

steps.title: Route registry with method and path
steps.description: Define a `Route` struct with `Method string`, `Path string`, and `Handler func(req map[string]string) (int, string)`. Create a `Gateway` with `routes []Route`. Implement `AddRoute(method, path string, handler func)`. Register a GET `/hello` route and print `"route registered"` with `fmt.Println("route registered")`.
hints: Store routes in a slice; matching iterates in order.
`Handler` receives parsed path params and returns status code + body.
Use `strings.ToUpper(method)` for normalization.

verification.successMessage: Route is registered in the gateway.
verification.failureMessage: AddRoute should add to the routes slice.

steps.title: Path matching with parameters
steps.description: Implement `match(path, pattern string) (map[string]string, bool)` that extracts path parameters. Pattern `/users/:id/posts/:postID` matches `/users/42/posts/7` returning `{"id": "42", "postID": "7"}`. Print the matched params for a sample request.
hints: Split both path and pattern by `/`.
If a segment starts with `:`, it's a parameter — capture the value.
If segments don't match and it's not a param, return false.

steps.title: Request transformation (headers)
steps.description: Add `TransformRequest func(headers map[string]string) map[string]string` to `Gateway`. Apply the transform to incoming headers before routing. For example, add `X-Gateway: true` to all requests. Print the transformed headers using `fmt.Printf("X-Gateway: %s", headers["X-Gateway"])`.
hints: Store `requestTransform` on the Gateway struct.
Call transform after matching the route, before the handler.
The handler receives the transformed headers.

verification.successMessage: Request headers are transformed before routing.
verification.failureMessage: TransformRequest should add/modify headers before the handler runs.

steps.title: Service aggregation (fan-out)
steps.description: Implement `Aggregate(routes []string, params map[string]string) []AggregateResult` that fans out requests to multiple downstream handlers concurrently using goroutines and `sync.WaitGroup`. Return each result with route ID and response. Print all aggregated results.
hints: Use `sync.WaitGroup` to wait for all goroutines.
Each goroutine calls the route handler and sends results via a channel.
`AggregateResult` has `RouteID string`, `StatusCode int`, `Body string`.

verification.successMessage: Service aggregation fans out and collects results.
verification.failureMessage: Aggregate should invoke multiple routes in parallel and collect responses.

steps.title: Response caching with TTL
steps.description: Add a cache layer: `CacheGet(key string) (string, bool)` and `CacheSet(key, value string, ttl time.Duration)` using `map[string]cacheEntry` where `cacheEntry` has `Body string` and `ExpiresAt time.Time`. Check cache before calling the handler. Print `"cache hit"` or `"cache miss"` on each request.
hints: Compute cache key from method + path + sorted params.
Check `time.Now().After(entry.ExpiresAt)` to detect expiry.
Use `sync.RWMutex` for concurrent cache access.

verification.failureMessage: First request should miss, subsequent requests within TTL should hit.

steps.title: Rate limiting per route
steps.description: Implement per-route rate limiting with a token bucket algorithm. Add `RateLimit int` (requests per second) to `Route`. Create a bucket per route: `allowRequest(routeID string) bool`. Return 429 status when rate exceeded. Print `"rate limited"` when the limit is hit.
hints: Token bucket: refill tokens at rate per second, max burst capacity.
Store `map[string]*TokenBucket` on the Gateway.
`TokenBucket` has `tokens float64` and `lastRefill time.Time`.

verification.successMessage: Rate limiting blocks requests over the limit.
verification.failureMessage: Requests exceeding the rate limit should return 429.

steps.title: Response composition
steps.description: Implement a response composer that aggregates multiple route responses into a single JSON-like payload. `ComposeResponse(results []AggregateResult) string` wraps results in `{"services": [...]}`. Print the composed JSON response using `fmt.Println(composeResponse(results))`.
hints: Use `encoding/json` or manual string building for the JSON output.
Each result becomes `{"id": "...", "status": N, "body": "..."}`.
Wrap all results in an outer object with a `services` key.

verification.failureMessage: Composed response should include all service results in a JSON structure.
